problem:
Given that a curve is defined parametrically as

$$
x=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2,\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,
$$

what are the ranges of $x$ and $y?$

feedback.problem:
Determine the graph of the following parametrically defined curve:

$$
x=7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\,\,y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi 
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to create a table of values and then sketch the curve. First, we work out the $x$-values using the formula $x=7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$ This gives

| **$\theta $** | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{6}$ | $\frac{\pi }{3}$ | $\frac{2\pi }{3}$ | $\pi $ | $\frac{4\pi }{3}$ | $\frac{5\pi }{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $7$ | $\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $\frac{7}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $-7$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{7}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $$ | $$ | $$ | $$ | $$ | $$ | $$ |

$$

$$

| **$\theta $** | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{6}$ | $\frac{\pi }{3}$ | $\frac{2\pi }{3}$ | $\pi $ | $\frac{4\pi }{3}$ | $\frac{5\pi }{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $7$ | $\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $\frac{7}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $-7$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{7}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $0$ | $\frac{5}{2}$ | $\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $0$ | $-\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $-\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$ |
